attributes.residual: THE BAR HOLDS AND IS NOW SCREENED AGAINST THE FULL EXISTING-CLASS SET, which HV's cap was not. NEW THIS RUN, AND THE PART THAT CHANGES THE PICTURE: the two refusal sites are NOT the same kind of thing, and instrumenting both (HV instrumented only the second) shows why the repair cannot help. Site +0x84, the un-repaired refusal: `hv_bypass.py game/sys/memcard drawMemCardMessage 0x84 0x24` prints NO path to +0x84 avoiding +0x24 (reached 9 of 204 words), i.e. the `li r26,0` definition at +0x24 DOMINATES the refusing use. By HV's own discriminator that is the REPAIRABLE class, which is exactly why the transposition relocates it. Site +0x1ec, the post-repair refusal: `hv_bypass.py ... 0x1ec 0xcc` prints a 93-word path terminating at `+0x1ec addi r3,r28,0`, so a path from entry reaches the refusing use while AVOIDING the definition that should bind it - the correspondence would rest on a caller-supplied callee-saved value and BOTH verifiers refuse CORRECTLY. The refusal is therefore a fact about the FUNCTION at site 2 and a fact about the CHECKER at site 1, and the repair only ever converts the first into the second. The invariance argument is unchanged and now applies to the value-equality mode too: a permutation window must be control-free, so no permutation stage can add, remove or redirect a CFG edge, so the bypass path at +0x1ec is invariant under every repair in the class. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT: source work in the memcard TU that makes our build colour the +0xcc web r25-equivalently. NOT eligible and deliberately not attempted: the third escape the refusal message names, `unproven_recolor_audit` - that is the UNPROVEN path, and under the standing governance mandate (11 unproven pins already queued for source-first remediation) authoring another one is not a lane decision.
